_comment: The roster rsb0t keeps in rsb0t-data/fleet.config.json. `rsb0t setup`, `rsb0t server` and `rsb0t account` write it for you; this file only shows the shape. It never holds a password: passwords are in credentialsFile (credentials.json beside the roster), written by the setup page or `rsb0t account add`. The roster is read leniently: an unknown or misspelt key is ignored, not an error, so read back what you change (`rsb0t server`, `rsb0t account list`).
_comment_key: Leave modulus and exponent out: the login key is read from <httpBase>client/client.js at every start, and read again after a response 6 in case the server changed it. Set them (decimal; `rsb0t server ADDRESS -modulus N -exponent N` does it) only when that file does not carry the key, for example for a local test engine from its data/config/private.pem. A pasted key is used as it is and never re-read.
_comment_paths: The data files a walking script needs. packPath is a collision pack (collision.lcnav[.gz]), locsPath a cmd/locbake output, configPath the server's config archive (cmd/cachecfgtest -save). All optional: an account with no script, or a script that does not walk, needs none of them.
_comment_worlds: worldList names the worlds the server has; `rsb0t server <one world's address>` fills it with the ones that answer. A world is another wsURL, derived by changing the leading wN. of the host. Each listed world is checked with one read-only GET of its /crc0 at start, and one that does not answer is reported, not fatal. Accounts pick a world with "world": N (0 or absent: the world wsURL names). An account refused with response 7 (world full) is moved to a listed world with room.
_comment_worlds_explicit: Only for a server whose world hosts are not wN.<site>: state each world's endpoints by hand, e.g. {"2": {"wsURL": "wss://game2.example-server.com/", "httpBase": "https://game2.example-server.com/"}}. `rsb0t server` drops these when the server is changed.
